text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's Council of Ministers failed to discuss legislation on working procedures for council due to Bosnian Serb representatives' refusal to stick to previously agreed agenda, co-chairman Haris Silajadzic says.
- Croatian Foreign Affairs Minister Mate Granic is due to visit Sarajevo on Friday to discuss formation of joint police force in Mostar region.
- Chairman of collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman may meet by end of June, says Ismet Grbo, spokesman of Party for Democratic Action.

- Bosnian authorities have sent evidence to the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia on atrocities committed by Serb soldiers in villages near Sarajevo in June 1992, newspaper reports without citing sources.
- Bosnia Serb entity's president, Biljana Plavsic, and president of the Moslem-Croat federation, Vladimir Soljic, discussed return of refugees in meeting held in Banja Luka.
- Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister, Edhem Bicakcic, says that federation parliament will adopt privatisation laws by end of June.
- Central European Initiative conference which begins in Sarajevo on Friday will discuss extention of the European Union and NATO as well as current sitaution in Bosnia and Albania.
- European Commission office in Sarajevo says it will sponsor 8 million ECU telecommunication project which will help rebuild telephone network between Bosnia's two entities.

- Gordon Bardos, a former NATO soldier who now works for Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, failed to show up at work after photos were published in a Sarajevo newspaper showing him kissing the Bosnian Serb flag while in his U.S. military uniform. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
